units.title: Ordinal numbers and dates (in / on)
notes: Ordinal numbers show order: first (1st), second (2nd), third (3rd), fourth (4th).
Most ordinals end in -th: sixth, tenth. Be careful with fifth, eighth, ninth, twelfth and twentieth.
Use on with days and dates: The party is on Saturday. My birthday is on 5th May.
Use in with months: My birthday is in July.

items.q: January is the ___ month of the year.
My birthday is ___ 3rd June.
Dad's birthday is ___ October.
There are eight candles on the cake. Today is my ___ birthday.
The party with balloons and sweets is ___ Saturday.
items.why: on + a day of the week

items.q: There are nine children in front of me. I am ___ in the line.
items.why: position in a line needs an ordinal number

items.q: Tom is nine today. It is his ___ birthday.
Christmas Day is on the ___ of December.
Which is the ___ letter of the alphabet? It is D.
March is the ___ (three) month of the year.
My sister is twelve today. It is her ___ (twelve) birthday.
items.why: twelve becomes twelfth (ve changes to f)

items.q: The party is on the ___ (twenty) of April.
Friday is the ___ (five) day of the school week.
Halloween is on the ___ (thirty-one) of October.
items.why: only the last number changes: thirty-first

items.q: This is my ___ (two) plate of crisps. The first one was very small!
My birthday is in 12th May.
We have a big party on December.
a: We have a big party in December.

items.q: Today is my sister's nine birthday.
a: Today is my sister's ninth birthday.

items.q: is / my / on / birthday / of / the first / August
a: My birthday is on the first of August.

items.q: party / in / the second / is / the / week / of March
a: The party is in the second week of March.

units.title: Telling the time; at and on
notes: Minutes 1 to 30 use past: It's ten past eight. It's quarter past eleven. It's half past four.
Minutes 31 to 59 use to and the next hour: It's twenty to seven. It's quarter to six.
Use at with times and on with days: I get up at seven o'clock. I play tennis on Fridays.
Questions: What time do you get up? What time does she go to bed?

items.q: It's 4:30. It's half ___ four.
items.why: 30 minutes after the hour is half past

items.q: It's 6:45. It's quarter ___ seven.
items.why: 15 minutes before seven is quarter to seven

items.q: I wake up ___ seven o'clock.
We don't go to school ___ Sundays.

items.why: minutes first, then past, then the hour

items.q: What time ___ she get up?
It's 9:00. It's nine ___.
items.why: we say o'clock for exact hours

items.q: It's 11:40. It's twenty ___ twelve.
items.why: 20 minutes before twelve is twenty to twelve

items.q: My brother ___ to bed at half past nine.
My dad ___ (get up) at six o'clock every day.
Anna ___ (take) a shower every morning before school.
What time ___ (do) your sister get dressed?
items.why: your sister is she, so does

items.q: I ___ (not/go) to bed late on Mondays. I have school on Tuesdays.
It's 3:15. It's ___ (quarter) three.
items.why: 15 minutes after the hour is quarter past

items.q: Tom ___ (put on) his shoes before school every morning.
I get up at the seven o'clock.
a: I get up at seven o'clock.

items.q: She plays tennis in Fridays.
My mum take off her shoes at home.
a: My mum takes off her shoes at home.

items.q: up / at / I / seven / wake / quarter / past
a: I wake up at quarter past seven.

items.q: time / you / what / do / go / to bed / on Fridays
a: What time do you go to bed on Fridays?

units.title: Possessive adjectives (my, your, his, her, its, our, their)
notes: I, my. You, your. He, his. She, her. It, its: She has got a cold. Her nose is red.
We, our. They, their: We love our doctor. They wash their hands.
his is for a boy or a man, her is for a girl or a woman: Tom and his sister, Anna and her brother.
The word never takes -s for plural things: their hands (not theirs hands).

items.q: My brother has got a headache. ___ head hurts.
items.why: my brother is he, so his

items.q: Lucy is ill. The doctor takes ___ temperature.
We wash ___ hands before lunch.
The children have got colds. ___ noses are running.
items.why: the children are they, so their

items.q: The cat has got a bad paw. It is licking ___ foot.
Open ___ mouth, please, Tom.
I have got a toothache. ___ tooth hurts a lot.
Dad cut ___ finger with a knife.
My grandparents are ill. I take soup to ___ house.
items.why: my grandparents are they, so their

items.q: Sara and I are ill, so ___ (we) grandmother brings us chicken soup.
items.why: Sara and I are we, so our

items.q: Ben has got an earache. The doctor looks at ___ (he) ear.
My sister is in bed because ___ (she) stomach hurts.
items.why: my sister is she, so her

items.q: The twins don't feel well. Mum takes ___ (they) temperature.
items.why: the twins are they, so their

items.q: I don't feel well and ___ (I) nose is running.
The dog is ill. It doesn't want ___ (it) food.
She has got a cough and his head hurts.
a: She has got a cough and her head hurts.

items.q: The boys are washing theirs hands.
a: The boys are washing their hands.
items.why: their never takes -s before a noun

items.q: Take you medicine, Anna.
is / mother / my / temperature / taking / my
a: My mother is taking my temperature.

items.q: their / the / wash / children / before / hands / lunch
a: The children wash their hands before lunch.
Before lunch the children wash their hands.
Before lunch, the children wash their hands.

units.title: Who and that (relative clauses)
notes: Use who for people: This is the girl who wears a red scarf.
Use that for animals and things: This is the coat that keeps me warm.
who and that join two ideas: The boy who has no gloves is cold.
Do not repeat the subject after who or that: The man who is wearing a hat (not who he is wearing).

items.q: This is the boy ___ has got a new winter coat.
I have got a scarf ___ is very long.
The woman ___ is wearing boots is my teacher.
These are the gloves ___ keep my hands warm.
The dog ___ lives next door wears a little jacket in winter.
The girl who ___ wearing tights is my sister.
items.why: the girl is one person, so is

items.q: The children who ___ in the snow have got red noses.
I like the jeans that ___ in the shop window.
The man who lives next door ___ a hat every day.
items.why: do not repeat the subject with he

items.q: The boy who ___ (sit) next to me at school always wears a green jacket.
items.why: the boy is he, so sits

items.q: Look! The girl who ___ (wear) the red dress now is my cousin.
I have got two coats that ___ (be) too small for me this winter.
items.why: two coats is plural, so are

items.q: Dad has got a jacket that ___ (have) four big pockets.
items.why: a jacket is it, so has

items.q: Autumn is the season that ___ (come) after summer.
items.why: the season is it, so comes

items.q: People who ___ (not/wear) a coat in winter get cold.
The girl who she has a blue scarf is my friend.
a: The girl who has a blue scarf is my friend.

items.q: I like the boots who are in the shop.
a: I like the boots that are in the shop.
I like the boots which are in the shop.

items.q: The man what sells hats is very nice.
a: The man who sells hats is very nice.
The man that sells hats is very nice.

items.q: who / the girl / gloves / is wearing / my sister / is
a: The girl who is wearing gloves is my sister.
My sister is the girl who is wearing gloves.

items.q: a coat / that / I / very warm / want / is
a: I want a coat that is very warm.

units.title: Present continuous (and present simple)
notes: am / is / are + verb-ing for things happening now: I am mixing the butter and sugar.
Negative and questions: She isn't cooking. Are you cutting the tomatoes? Yes, I am.
Spelling: make, making (no e). cut, cutting (double t). mix, mixing.
Use the present simple for habits: We cook pasta every Friday.

items.q: Look! Dad ___ pasta in a big pot.
items.why: Look! means now, so is + verb-ing

items.q: We ___ the tomatoes now.
___ you making a cake?
items.why: questions start with am, is or are

items.q: I ___ the sugar and the butter at the moment.
Mum ___ using the oven now. It is cold.
items.why: Mum is she, so isn't + verb-ing

items.q: We ___ pasta every Sunday.
items.why: every Sunday is a habit, so present simple

items.q: What ___ the children doing in the kitchen?
items.why: the children are they, so are

items.q: Is your brother tasting the soup? Yes, he ___.
Be careful! You ___ a very big knife.
Look at Tom! He ___ (cut up) the peppers.
items.why: now, and cut doubles the t

items.q: I can't help you now. I ___ (clean up) the kitchen.
The children ___ (not/make) a cake now. They are making biscuits.
items.why: they + aren't + verb-ing, make loses the e

items.q: My sister ___ (cook) dinner every Saturday.
items.why: every Saturday is a habit, so present simple

items.q: Mmm! Right now Dad ___ (taste) the tomato soup.
items.why: right now, and taste loses the e

items.q: What are you doing? We ___ (roll out) the pasta.
She is cook pasta now.
They making a salad at the moment.
a: They are making a salad at the moment.
They're making a salad at the moment.

items.q: Do you mixing the butter now?
a: Are you mixing the butter now?
items.why: present continuous questions use are, not do

items.q: putting / is / in / the bowl / sugar / my brother
a: My brother is putting sugar in the bowl.

items.q: you / in / are / the oven / what / cooking
a: What are you cooking in the oven?

units.title: Have got and be; had (past of have)
notes: Use be for age and for how you are or feel: I am nine. She is tall. We are hungry.
Use have got for hair, eyes and things: He has got curly hair. They have got brown eyes.
he / she / it + has got. I / you / we / they + have got.
The past of have got is had (not had got): I had long hair last year.

items.q: My sister ___ long blonde hair.
items.why: hair needs have got, and she takes has

items.q: I ___ ten years old.
My grandad ___ black hair when he was young.
items.why: past of have got is had

items.q: Tom and Ben ___ short brown hair.
items.why: Tom and Ben are they, so have got

items.q: The baby ___ hungry.
___ your mum got curly hair?
items.why: your mum is she, so Has ... got

items.q: Last year I ___ very short hair. Now it is long.
items.why: last year is past, so had

items.q: Have you got red hair? No, I ___.
Her hair ___ straight and black.
My dad ___ (have got) grey hair now.
items.why: my dad is he, so has got

items.q: When my mum was a girl, she ___ (have) long curly hair.
I can't walk any more. I ___ (be) very tired.
My brother ___ (not/have got) blond hair. His hair is brown.
Two years ago my friends ___ (have) short hair.
items.why: two years ago is past, so had

items.q: My cousin ___ (be) eight years old and she has got red hair.
I have got nine years old.
items.why: age uses be, not have got

items.q: She have got curly hair.
My grandmother had got red hair before.
a: My grandmother had red hair before.
items.why: the past is had, without got

items.q: got / has / long straight / my / hair / teacher
a: My teacher has got long straight hair.

items.q: when / I / hair / had / I / blonde / was / a baby
a: I had blonde hair when I was a baby.
When I was a baby, I had blonde hair.
When I was a baby I had blonde hair.

units.title: Past simple: was / were and went
notes: was with I / he / she / it, were with you / we / they: The museum was big. We were happy.
Negative: wasn't, weren't. Questions: Was the cinema open? Were you at the library?
The past of go is went: We went to the swimming pool yesterday.
After didn't and Did use go (not went): I didn't go. Did you go?

items.q: Yesterday we ___ at the museum all morning.
The supermarket ___ closed last Sunday.
items.why: the supermarket is it, so was

items.q: Last Saturday I ___ to the cinema with my cousins.
We didn't ___ to the swimming pool yesterday.
___ you at the library yesterday afternoon?
items.why: you + were, and no verb go here

items.q: ___ she go to the bank last Friday?
items.why: past questions with a verb use Did

items.q: The hotel ___ expensive. It was very cheap.
items.why: the hotel is it, so wasn't

items.q: Were they at the sports centre? No, they ___.
Did you go to the bus stop? Yes, I ___.
Last summer my family ___ (go) to a hotel near the beach.
I ___ (be) at the library yesterday after school.
My friends ___ (not/be) at the sports centre last night.
Anna ___ (not/go) to the museum last week. She was ill.
Where ___ (be) you yesterday morning?
Did your dad ___ (go) to the bank yesterday?
We didn't went to the restaurant last night.
a: We didn't go to the restaurant last night.
We did not go to the restaurant last night.

items.q: The children was at the swimming pool yesterday.
a: The children were at the swimming pool yesterday.
items.why: the children are they, so were

items.q: Yesterday I go to the supermarket with my mum.
a: Yesterday I went to the supermarket with my mum.

items.q: to / did / the cinema / you / last / go / Friday
a: Did you go to the cinema last Friday?

items.q: we / at / yesterday / weren't / the museum
a: We weren't at the museum yesterday.
Yesterday we weren't at the museum.
Yesterday, we weren't at the museum.

units.title: Past simple: regular verbs (-ed)
notes: Add -ed for the past: walk, walked. look, looked. We walked in the forest yesterday.
Verb ends in -e: add -d (live, lived). Consonant + y: change to -ied (cry, cried).
Short verbs like stop and drop double the last letter: stopped, dropped.
Negative and questions use didn't / Did + base verb: I didn't walk. Did you walk?

items.q: Yesterday we ___ along the path to the pond.
items.why: yesterday is past, so verb + ed

items.q: The deer ___ at the stream to drink some water.
The baby swan ___ because it was cold.
My grandparents ___ in a small village when they were young.
items.why: when they were young is past

items.q: We didn't ___ the mountain last weekend.
___ you visit the forest last Saturday?
The path was long, but we ___ at the village at six o'clock.
Did they walk up the hill? No, they ___.
Where did the swans ___ last winter?
Last Sunday we ___ (climb) a big hill near the village.
items.why: last Sunday is past, so verb + ed

items.q: Yesterday I ___ (try) to catch a butterfly in the field.
The rain ___ (stop) an hour ago, so we went for a walk.
We ___ (not/cross) the stream yesterday because it was too deep.
Last night the farmer ___ (close) the gate of the field.
My sister ___ (enjoy) the walk in the forest yesterday.
We didn't walked to the pond yesterday.
a: We didn't walk to the pond yesterday.
We did not walk to the pond yesterday.

items.q: Last week I visit my grandma in the village.
a: Last week I visited my grandma in the village.
items.why: last week is past, so visited

items.q: We plaied football in the field yesterday.
a: We played football in the field yesterday.
items.why: vowel + y does not change: played

items.q: in / we / yesterday / the forest / walked
a: We walked in the forest yesterday.
Yesterday we walked in the forest.
Yesterday, we walked in the forest.

items.q: look / did / the swans / you / the pond / at / on
a: Did you look at the swans on the pond?

units.title: Comparatives and superlatives
notes: Comparative: adjective + -er + than: A zebra is faster than a panda.
Superlative: the + adjective + -est: The giraffe is the tallest animal.
Spelling: big, bigger, the biggest. happy, happier, the happiest.
Irregular: good, better, the best. bad, worse, the worst.

items.q: A zebra is ___ than a penguin.
The cheetah is the ___ animal in the world.
items.why: the + -est for number one in a group

items.q: An elephant is bigger ___ a skunk.
A rabbit's fur is ___ than a dog's fur.
The giraffe has got ___ longest neck of all the animals.
My dog is ___ than my cat.
Pandas are good climbers, but monkeys are ___.
A horse's tail is long, but a monkey's tail is ___.
The monkey is the ___ animal in the zoo. It makes everyone laugh.
A tiger's claws are ___ (sharp) than a cat's claws.
The blue whale is the ___ (big) animal in the world.
items.why: the + -est, and big doubles the g

items.q: A skunk's tail is ___ (short) than a zebra's tail.
My puppy is ___ (happy) than my old cat.
The rhino has got the ___ (strong) horn of all the animals.
I think snakes are the ___ (bad) pets in the world!
items.why: bad is irregular: worse, the worst

items.q: A panda is more big than a skunk.
a: A panda is bigger than a skunk.

items.q: The elephant is stronger that the zebra.
a: The elephant is stronger than the zebra.

items.q: The penguin is funniest bird in the zoo.
a: The penguin is the funniest bird in the zoo.

items.q: is / the / tallest / the giraffe / in the zoo / animal
a: The giraffe is the tallest animal in the zoo.
The tallest animal in the zoo is the giraffe.

items.q: is / than / she / faster / him / much
a: She is much faster than him.
